A `.bind()` call, an arrow function or a function expression in a prop creates a new function on every render. The child sees a prop that changed, so `React.memo` and `PureComponent` can't skip its render, and an effect that depends on the function runs again.

The rule also follows a prop back to a `const` or a function declared inside the component.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/jsx-no-bind" = "error" # or "warn"
```

Every option, set to its default:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"react/jsx-no-bind" = ["error", {
  allowArrowFunctions = false,
  allowFunctions = false,
  allowBind = false,
  ignoreRefs = false,
  ignoreDOMComponents = false,
}]
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```jsx
function Toolbar({ onSave, doc }) {
  const handleReset = () => doc.reset();

  return (
    <div>
      <Button onClick={() => onSave(doc)} />
      <Button onClick={doc.print.bind(doc)} />
      <Button onClick={handleReset} />
    </div>
  );
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```jsx
function Toolbar({ onSave, doc }) {
  const handleSave = useCallback(() => onSave(doc), [onSave, doc]);

  return <Button onClick={handleSave} />;
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `allowArrowFunctions` | `false` | Allow arrow functions. |
| `allowFunctions` | `false` | Allow `function` expressions and declarations. |
| `allowBind` | `false` | Allow `.bind()`. |
| `ignoreRefs` | `false` | Don't check the `ref` prop. |
| `ignoreDOMComponents` | `false` | Don't check DOM elements such as `<button>`. They're never memoized, so a new function costs them nothing. |

With `ignoreDOMComponents`, components are still checked:

{/* good {"options": [{"ignoreDOMComponents": true}]} */}
```jsx
const button = <button onClick={() => save(doc)}>Save</button>;
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"ignoreDOMComponents": true}]} */}
```jsx
const button = <Button onClick={() => save(doc)}>Save</Button>;
```

## When not to use it

A new function only costs something if the child is memoized or uses the function as a dependency. In most other code an inline arrow function is fine and easier to read. The React Compiler also memoizes these functions for you.
